description: Solo team building Field Shift, a decision-support tool that helps farmers compare crop rotations using NASA climate data.
summary: Field Shift is a decision-support tool that helps farmers explore crop rotations that protect soil and save water as the climate changes. A farmer picks any field on Earth. The app loads 20 years of NASA POWER data (rain, temperature and root-zone soil wetness), shows how the climate has changed there, and projects that trend forward. It then compares three rotations, including the current one, scored against the farmer's own priorities: water saving, soil health, erosion control and income. Each option explains why it was suggested, what evidence supports it, the risks, and the data gaps. This matters because farmers face less predictable rain and warmer seasons, and a rotation that works in one place can fail in another. Field Shift supports farmer judgment and never replaces local agronomists. Next steps: add SMAP, ECOSTRESS, OpenET and SRTM layers, plus local soil and market data. AI tools helped build the video;
details:
What it does: Field Shift is a web tool that helps a farmer compare crop rotations under changing climate conditions. The farmer picks a field (a preset region, latitude and longitude, or the device location). The app loads 20 years (2005–2024) of monthly NASA POWER data for that point: rainfall (PRECTOTCORR), air temperature (T2M, T2M_MAX) and root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT). It then shows yearly rainfall with a trend line, the change in rain and temperature per decade, and a typical year with frost-risk months highlighted.

How it works: The observed trend can be projected 20 years ahead with one button, or the farmer can set rainfall and warming scenarios manually. Three rotations are compared: the farmer's current rotation, an adapted version (adds a legume and a cover crop, replaces bare fallow), and a resilient option chosen for the local climate (heat-tolerant or cold-tolerant crops). Each rotation is scored from 0 to 100 against the farmer's own priorities: water saving, soil health, erosion control and income. Scores shift with water stress calculated from soil wetness and the climate scenario. Each card explains why the rotation was suggested, which NASA data supports it, the risks to review, and the information gaps.

Benefits and impact: Farmers can see how their own field's climate has changed and test rotation ideas before committing land and money. Fields left bare are flagged, and options that add nitrogen-fixing crops and ground cover are rewarded.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (single page, no server), NASA POWER API, SVG charts, canvas animation. Hosted on GitHub Pages.

Creativity: A starry-night interface with shooting stars, and the story of one farmer, Jon, to make climate data personal.

Factors considered: The tool supports farmer judgment and does not replace local agronomists. Crop traits are simplified estimates. Soil tests, local prices and pest history are not yet included, and the interface says so on every option.

Next steps: Add SMAP soil moisture, ECOSTRESS heat stress, OpenET water use, SRTM slope and erosion zones, and local soil and market inputs.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) – monthly rainfall, temperature and root-zone soil wetness
NASA POWER API – monthly point data (2005–2024)
